group_results.reason: The new dump depth guard supports clean failure for constructed over-depth values, but the entry only dumps values returned by json_loadb. Parsing rejects the extra depth before either dump call.

build.reason: The supplied wrapper delegates the build to test/ossfuzz/ossfuzz.sh; its contents and a build result are not supplied. Build status is not decisive to the established state blocker.

input.reason: The entry accepts command bytes and JSON text, but mandatory json_loadb parsing cannot produce the constructed over-depth value needed by the dump guard.

lifecycle.reason: On the relevant route, loading closes its lexer, each dump wrapper closes its temporary state, and the entry frees string output and decrements the loaded value.

control_flow.reason: A parse failure returns from the entry before either dump mode; both modes otherwise use the same parsed object.

accepted.requirement: The JSON dump operation must be able to receive a supported, over-depth json_t so its clean depth-limit failure can be exercised.
accepted.target_route: A finite command prefix selects a dump mode and supplies JSON text. The entry passes the text to json_loadb, returns if loading fails, and passes only the loaded value to json_dumps or json_dump_callback.
accepted.failure_condition: A constructed nested value can reach do_dump at depth JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH and fail cleanly. JSON text yielding that child requires parse_value beyond JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH, so json_loadb returns NULL before dumping.
accepted.alternative_paths: JSON_DECODE_ANY changes the permitted root type and JSON_DISABLE_EOF_CHECK changes trailing-input handling; neither bypasses parse_value's depth check. Both dump modes use the same loaded value, and the complete entry has no later construction or mutation route.
